test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 24 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is true with respect to regeneration?

options.text: No organism on earth has the ability to regenerate.
Regeneration and reproduction are the same process with different names in all organisms.
Regeneration gives rise to a totally new organism.
Regeneration is not the same as reproduction.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Regeneration is not the same as reproduction.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Regeneration is a biological process where organisms replace or restore lost or damaged tissues, organs, or body parts.
 
• While some organisms can regenerate parts of their bodies, this process does not always result in the creation of a new organism.
 
• Regeneration is distinct from reproduction, which involves the creation of a new organism from one or two parent organisms.
 
• Examples of organisms with high regenerative capabilities include starfish, planarians, and certain species of lizards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Planarians:** Flatworms known for their remarkable regenerative abilities, capable of regrowing entire bodies from small segments.
 
• **Autotomy:** A defense mechanism in some animals, such as lizards, where they shed a body part (e.g., tail) to escape predators, which can later regenerate.
 
• **Stem Cells:** Undifferentiated cells that play a critical role in the regeneration process by differentiating into various cell types to replace damaged tissues.
 
• **Asexual Reproduction:** A mode of reproduction that does not involve the fusion of gametes, resulting in offspring genetically identical to the parent, distinct from regeneration.
 
• **Epimorphosis:** A type of regeneration where cells proliferate at the site of injury and differentiate to form new tissues, commonly seen in amphibians.
